category: Molecular Flow Module and Granular Flow Module: Rarefied Gas and Discrete Element Grain Flow
description: Interfaces and features of the COMSOL Molecular Flow Module (Free Molecular Flow with the angular coefficient method and Transitional Flow with the lattice Boltzmann method) for vacuum systems, and of the Granular Flow Module (discrete element method for grains: contact models, releases, walls, accumulators, grain datasets), with verified Java type strings and property names (COMSOL 6.4).

tools.name: Free Molecular Flow (fmf)
tools.description: Interface for gas flow in the free molecular regime (Knudsen number >> 1) where molecules interact with surfaces rather than with each other: the angular coefficient method computes incident molecular fluxes by integrating diffusely re-emitted (Knudsen cosine law) fluxes over visible surfaces, giving pressure, number density and heat flux on boundaries. Transient solves are quasistatic. It is used for high- and ultrahigh-vacuum systems, load locks, ion implanters, differential pumping and outgassing studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Rarefied Flow > Free Molecular Flow (fmf); Java: physics().create("fmf", "FreeMolecularFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Species
parameters.description: One or several gas species (Dependent Variables section); each has incident flux G.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Molecular Flow (fmfp1), Surface Temperature (st1), Wall (wall1), Initial Values.

tools.notes: Requires the Molecular Flow Module. Only surfaces are meshed for the flux computation; use constant shape function results with No Refinement in plots.

tools.name: Integration Settings: Hemicube and Direct Area Integration (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Interface-level settings controlling how the incoming molecular flux on each element is computed. Hemicube (default) renders z-buffered views of the geometry to account for shadowing, with an integration resolution (default 256) whose cost grows quadratically; Direct area integration with an integration order (default 4) is fast only for simple unobstructed geometries. Axisymmetric models also need the number of integration sectors.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Integration Settings
tools.example:
// GUI: Free Molecular Flow > Integration Settings > Integration resolution = 512 for geometries with narrow gaps
// Application Library: Molecular_Flow_Module/Benchmarks/s_bend_benchmark
tools.notes: Sharp angles and small gaps need higher resolution and finer meshes; chamfering acute edges helps.

tools.name: Molecular Flow (Free Molecular Flow Domain Node)
tools.description: Default domain node of Free Molecular Flow defining the mean molar mass of each species, which is needed to compute pressure, number density and heat flux on boundaries from the molecular fluxes.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Molecular Flow (fmfp1)
tools.example:
// GUI: Free Molecular Flow > Molecular Flow 1 > Mean molar mass = 0.002[kg/mol] (H2)
model.component("comp1").physics("fmf").feature("fmfp1");
tools.notes: Species do not interact in the gas phase, so adding species barely increases cost.

tools.name: Wall and Outgassing Wall (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Wall feature for vacuum-system surfaces: a plain Wall re-emits all incident molecules diffusely (J = G); an Outgassing wall adds an outgassing flux given directly, as SCCM, mass flux, total mass flow or thermal desorption rate (e.g., 3e-12 torr·l/(cm²·s)). Other wall types handle adsorption/desorption and deposition.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Wall; Java: physics("fmf").feature("wall1").set("BCType", "OutgassingWall")

parameters.name: StandardFlowRateDefinedBy
parameters.description: StandardRho or StandardP for SCCM conversion.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Adsorption/Desorption and Deposition Walls (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Wall types for transient surface processes: Adsorption/Desorption uses a sticking coefficient and desorption rate per species and tracks the adsorbed amount fmf.n_ads, so pump-down curves with water desorption can be computed; Deposition accumulates a deposited film thickness from the incident flux and film density, for coating and CVD uniformity studies.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Wall > Wall type: Adsorption/Desorption or Deposition; Java: feature("wall2").set("BCType", "AdsorptionDesorption")

parameters.name: rho_film / h_film_0
parameters.description: Deposited film density and initial thickness.

tools.notes: Adsorption/desorption requires a time-dependent study.

tools.name: Vacuum Pump (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Boundary representing a high-vacuum pump inlet (turbomolecular, cryogenic or diffusion pump): the emitted flux is J = G - J_pump with the pumped flux given directly, as a fraction of incident molecules (capture probability, default 0.8) or from a pump speed S (default 500 l/s) converted with the pump area.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Vacuum Pump; Java: physics("fmf").create("pmp1", "VacuumPump", 2)

parameters.name: Channel thickness
parameters.description: 2D models: out-of-plane thickness for the pump area.

tools.notes: Ensure the specified pumped flux never becomes negative. Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Reservoir (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Opening to a large adjacent chamber at a specified pressure or number density: the effusing incoming flux follows Knudsen's law for a Maxwellian gas. The pressure at the opening can differ from the reservoir value because effusion selects faster molecules.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Reservoir; Java: physics("fmf").create("res1", "Reservoir", 2); feature("res1").set("p0", ...)
tools.notes: Valid when the opening is small compared with the mean free path in the reservoir.

tools.name: Total Vacuum and Diffuse Flux (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Total Vacuum sets the emitted flux to zero, representing an opening to a much lower-pressure region or a perfect pump; Diffuse Flux emits a user-specified molecular flux with a cosine distribution (directly, SCCM, mass flux or total mass flow), representing gas inlets such as leak valves or effusion sources.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Total Vacuum / Diffuse Flux; Java: physics("fmf").create("tv1", "TotalVacuum", 2); create("df1", "DiffuseFlux", 2)

parameters.name: Outgoing flux (Diffuse Flux)
parameters.description: Specify directly, Number of SCCM units, Mass flux, Total mass flow.

tools.notes: Transmission probabilities of tubes are obtained with a Reservoir at the inlet and Total Vacuum at the outlet.

tools.name: Surface Temperature and Evaporation (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Surface Temperature defines the temperature of emitting surfaces (user value or from a Heat Transfer interface), which affects the emission speed, pressure and heat flux; Evaporation defines an evaporative source per species from vapor pressure and evaporation coefficient, typically used with a Surface Temperature on a heated crucible.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Surface Temperature (st1) / Evaporation; Java: physics("fmf").create("evap1", "Evaporation", 2)

parameters.name: Temperature T
parameters.description: Default 293.15 K or from another interface.

tools.notes: Couple to Heat Transfer in Solids for nonisothermal vacuum components.

tools.name: Number Density Reconstruction (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Features that compute the molecular number density inside the gas volume (domains, boundaries, edges or points) during the solve from the surface fluxes, since the angular coefficient method only solves on surfaces. An operator comp1.fmf.nop_G(x,y,z) evaluates the number density at arbitrary points in postprocessing.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Number Density Reconstruction (domain/boundary/edge/point); operator fmf.nop_<species>(x,y,z)
tools.notes: Domain reconstruction is expensive; restrict it to regions of interest.

tools.name: Symmetry and Plane Symmetry (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Symmetry specifies planar reflection planes (up to several perpendicular planes) or start/end planes of sector symmetry for the molecular flux integration, reducing model size; only one Symmetry node per interface is allowed and the selected faces must be coplanar per plane. The older Plane Symmetry node is obsolete.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Symmetry (msym); Java: physics("fmf").create("msym1", "Symmetry", 2)

parameters.name: Symmetry type
parameters.description: One, two or three reflection planes, or sector symmetry (with/without reflection).

parameters.name: Plane selections
parameters.description: Coplanar exterior boundaries for each plane.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("fmf").create("msym1", "Symmetry", 2);
// GUI: First reflection plane: boundaries in the xz-plane
tools.notes: Do not combine Symmetry with the obsolete Plane Symmetry node.

tools.name: Pressure versus Number Density and Vacuum Gauge Readings (Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Guideline for comparing simulations with vacuum gauges: in molecular flow the ideal gas relation p = n k_B T is only approximate, COMSOL defines pressure as the normal force on surfaces and number density as molecules per volume. Direct gauges (diaphragm) measure pressure, while indirect gauges (ionization, Pirani) effectively measure number density, so n k_B T from the simulation should be compared with their readings.
tools.usage: Reference (Molecular Flow Module User's Guide > Experimental Measurements of Number Density/Pressure); evaluate fmf pressure on walls or reconstructed number density at the gauge location

parameters.name: Indirect gauges
parameters.description: Compare with n k_B T at the gauge point.

tools.example:
// Gauge at (0.2,0,0.1): Global Evaluation of comp1.fmf.nop_G(0.2,0,0.1)*k_B_const*293.15[K]
// Application Library: Molecular_Flow_Module/Benchmarks/rotating_plate (case where p = n k T fails)
tools.notes: The Molecular Flow Module has no dedicated gauge feature; gauges are represented by boundaries or reconstruction points.

tools.name: Multiple Species (Free Molecular Flow)
tools.description: Free Molecular Flow can solve several gas species at once (added in the Dependent Variables section) at little extra cost because molecules do not collide in the gas; species can interact on surfaces, e.g., sharing adsorption sites or reacting in CVD. Each species gets its own molar mass, fluxes and boundary settings.
tools.usage: Free Molecular Flow > Dependent Variables > Number of species; species-specific inputs appear in each feature

parameters.name: Per-species boundary inputs
parameters.description: Outgassing, sticking, pump capture, reservoir pressure.

tools.example:
// GUI: Free Molecular Flow > Dependent Variables > Number of species = 2 (SiH4, H2)
// Application Library: Molecular_Flow_Module/Industrial_Applications/uhv_cvd
tools.notes: Needed whenever adsorption/desorption involves several gases.

tools.name: Transitional Flow (tran)
tools.description: Interface for isothermal rarefied gas flow across all Knudsen numbers, and the tool of choice for the transitional regime (0.1 < Kn < 10): it solves the Boltzmann BGK equation with a lattice Boltzmann/discrete velocity method using a Gauss–Hermite velocity quadratures DnQm, with diffuse wall reflection. Unlike DSMC it has no statistical noise, which suits low-speed flows in MEMS, vacuum and gas-sensor devices.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Rarefied Flow > Transitional Flow (tran); Java: physics().create("tran", "TransitionalFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Quadrature
parameters.description: Predefined DXQY lattices (X dimensions, Y velocities); dependent variables tran.f1..tran.fn.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Flow Properties, Wall, Continuity on Interior Boundary, Initial Values.

tools.notes: Requires the Molecular Flow Module; 2D and 3D; single species, isothermal only. After changing the quadrature, delete and regenerate the solver configuration.

tools.name: Flow Properties (Transitional Flow)
tools.description: Domain node of Transitional Flow defining dynamic viscosity (sets the BGK relaxation time), temperature and mean molar mass, which determine relaxation time, characteristic molecular speed and molecular mass. It also defines result variables such as velocity tran.ux/uy/uz, number density tran.n, density tran.rho and mean free path tran.lambda.
tools.usage: Transitional Flow > Flow Properties (tranp1)

parameters.name: mu
parameters.description: Dynamic viscosity (from material or user defined).

tools.notes: The BGK relaxation time reproduces viscosity but not thermal conductivity simultaneously, hence the isothermal restriction.

tools.name: Velocity Quadrature and Mesh Independence (Transitional Flow)
tools.description: The Transitional Flow interface has a mesh in physical space and one in velocity space (the Gauss–Hermite quadrature). Near the slip regime small quadratures and fine physical meshes suffice; toward free molecular flow larger quadratures are needed while coarser meshes are acceptable. Accurate results must not change when the quadrature is enlarged or the mesh refined.
tools.usage: Transitional Flow > Quadrature setting; mesh refinement study

parameters.name: Element order
parameters.description: Quadratic by default for the distribution functions.

tools.example: // Convergence check: solve with D2Q16 and a larger 2D quadrature, compare mass flow through the channel
tools.notes: Each quadrature velocity adds a dependent variable, so memory grows linearly with the quadrature size.

tools.name: Wall, Inlet and Outlet (Transitional Flow)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of Transitional Flow: Wall re-emits incident molecules diffusely with the equilibrium distribution of a stationary or moving wall; Inlet and Outlet (Navier–Stokes limit) prescribe normal velocity, pressure, density or number density at openings.
tools.usage: Transitional Flow > Wall (wall1) / Inlet / Outlet; Java: physics("tran").create("inl1", "Inlet", 1)

parameters.name: Wall boundary condition
parameters.description: Stationary wall or Moving wall (velocity u_w).

parameters.name: Inlet/Outlet condition
parameters.description: Velocity U0, Pressure p0, Density ρ0 or Number density n0.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").create("inl1", "Inlet", 1);
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").feature("inl1").selection().set(new int[]{1});
tools.notes: For openings in the molecular flow limit use Reservoir, Diffuse Flux, Total Vacuum or High Vacuum Pump instead.

tools.name: High Vacuum Pump (Transitional Flow)
tools.description: Pump boundary for the Transitional Flow interface in the molecular limit (Kn > 10): the pumped flux is specified directly, as a fraction of incident molecules or by a pump speed, emitting J = G - J_pump. It models turbomolecular or diffusion pump inlets.
tools.usage: Transitional Flow > High Vacuum Pump; Java: physics("tran").create("hvp1", "HighVacuumPump", 1)

parameters.name: Specify pump flux
parameters.description: Directly, Fraction of incident molecules or Pump speed.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").create("hvp1", "HighVacuumPump", 1);
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").feature("hvp1").selection().set(new int[]{7});
tools.notes: Keep the pumped flux non-negative.

tools.name: Outgassing Wall, Reservoir, Diffuse Flux and Total Vacuum (Transitional Flow)
tools.description: Molecular-limit boundary conditions of Transitional Flow: Outgassing Wall adds an outgassing flux (directly, SCCM, mass flux or total mass flow) to diffuse re-emission; Reservoir represents effusion from a large vessel at given pressure or number density; Diffuse Flux emits a prescribed cosine-law flux; Total Vacuum emits nothing.
tools.usage: Transitional Flow > Outgassing Wall (ogw) / Reservoir (res) / Diffuse Flux (df) / Total Vacuum (tv); Java type ids OutgassingWall, Reservoir, DiffuseFlux, TotalVacuum

parameters.name: Outgassing flux
parameters.description: Directly, Number of SCCM units, Mass flux or Total mass flow.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").create("ogw1", "OutgassingWall", 1);
model.component("comp1").physics("tran").feature("ogw1").selection().set(new int[]{3, 4});
tools.notes: Valid in the molecular flow limit (Kn > 10) of the transitional solver.

tools.name: Granular Flow (gran)
tools.description: Discrete element method (DEM) interface computing the motion of individual spherical grains by Newton's laws for translation and rotation, with soft-sphere contact forces between grains and between grains and walls. It models powders, bulk solids and particulate processes: hoppers and silo discharge, angle of repose, packing, mixing drums, ribbon mixers, screw conveyors, vibrating sieves and powder spreading for additive manufacturing.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Granular Flow (gran); Java: physics().create("gran", "GranularFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Contact force model
parameters.description: Linear elastic, Hertz–MD (default) or Hertz–MD with adhesion; optional van der Waals force.

parameters.name: Rotational resistance model
parameters.description: Constant torque, Varying torque (default) or None.

parameters.name: Additional variables
parameters.description: Compute grain temperature, conductive heat transfer, coordination numbers.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Grain Properties (gp1), Wall (wp1), Contact Between Grains (cbg1), Contact with Walls (cww1), Gravity (gf1).

tools.notes: Requires the Granular Flow Module (new in 6.3). Only explicit time stepping (default classical Runge–Kutta) is supported; verified type string GranularFlow, default tag gran.

tools.name: Grain Properties (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Node defining a grain species: density, Young's modulus with Poisson's ratio or shear modulus (Hertz–MD models), specific heat and thermal conductivity (when temperatures are computed) and grain diameter. Additional Grain Properties nodes (global) define further species for mixtures and size distributions.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Grain Properties (gp1); additional species: Java physics("gran").create("gp2", "GrainPropertiesOther", -1)

parameters.name: Eg / nug / Gg
parameters.description: Young's modulus (100 GPa), Poisson's ratio (0.1) or shear modulus (45.45 GPa).

tools.notes: Property keys and type ids verified in COMSOL 6.4. Material values can come from the granular material library.

tools.name: Wall (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Boundary node defining wall material properties (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio or shear modulus), thermal condition (specified temperature or insulated) and rigid-body wall motion: fixed, translation, rotation or translation and rotation with constant, general or user-defined angular velocity. Moving walls drive mixers, drums, rollers, screws and sieves.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Wall (wp1); Java: physics("gran").create("wp2", "WallProperties", 2)

parameters.name: RotationType / omegaw / eax / rbp
parameters.description: ConstantAngularVelocity, GeneralAngularVelocity or UserDefined; axis and base point.

tools.notes: Java type id is WallProperties (GUI label Wall). Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Contact Between Grains (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Global node with grain–grain contact pair properties: normal and tangential spring constants (linear elastic model), normal and tangential coefficients of restitution, sliding, rolling and twisting friction coefficients, interface energy for adhesion and van der Waals cutoff distances. The default node applies to all pairs; additional nodes override properties for selected species pairs.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Contact Between Grains (cbg1); Java: physics("gran").create("cbg2", "ContactBetweenGrains", -1)

parameters.name: kn / kt
parameters.description: Normal/tangential stiffness (linear elastic model, default 10 MN/m).

parameters.name: mus / mur / mutw
parameters.description: Sliding, rolling and twisting friction coefficients.

parameters.name: gammaij / Dmin / Dmax
parameters.description: Interface energy density and van der Waals distances.

tools.notes: Friction coefficients are the main calibration parameters for bulk behavior (angle of repose, flow rate).

tools.name: Contact with Walls (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Global node with grain–wall contact pair properties (restitution, stiffness, sliding/rolling/twisting friction, adhesion), applied to all pairs by default or to selected grain species, wall types or manual grain–wall pairs.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Contact with Walls (cww1); Java: physics("gran").create("cww2", "ContactWithWalls", -1)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: All pairs, walls with selected grain types, grains with selected wall types, or Manual.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("cww2", "ContactWithWalls", -1);
// GUI: Selection = Manual: Wall 2 with Grain Properties 1, sliding friction 0.3
tools.notes: Type id verified in COMSOL 6.4 (global feature, dimension -1).

tools.name: Gravity (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Default global node applying gravitational force to all grains; the acceleration vector defaults to g_const downward (-y in 2D, -z in 3D) and can point in any direction, for example to model inclined chutes by tilting gravity.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Gravity (gf1, type GravityForce)
tools.example:
// GUI: Granular Flow > Gravity 1 > g = {g_const*sin(30[deg]), 0, -g_const*cos(30[deg])} for a 30 degree chute
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").feature("gf1");
tools.notes: Only one Gravity node per model. Java type id GravityForce (verified).

tools.name: Contact Force Models: Linear Elastic, Hertz–MD, JKR Adhesion, van der Waals (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Soft-sphere contact models of the Granular Flow interface: Linear elastic (constant spring and damping coefficients), Hertz–MD (Hertz normal and Mindlin–Deresiewicz tangential forces with stiffness from material properties and overlap), Hertz–MD with adhesion (JKR model with tensile adhesive force and cutoff distance), plus an optional van der Waals attraction important for grains below about 10 µm.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Force > Contact force model; Compute van der Waals force checkbox

parameters.name: Hertz–MD
parameters.description: E, ν (or G), restitution; nonlinear stiffness ∝ sqrt(overlap).

tools.example:
// GUI: Granular Flow > Force > Contact force model = Hertz-MD with adhesion; Compute van der Waals force = on (fine cohesive powders)
// Application Library: Granular_Flow_Module/Transport/powder_spreading
tools.notes: The suggested time step (gran.ts) depends on the contact model (spring-mass or Rayleigh criterion).

tools.name: Rotational Resistance Models (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Rolling (2D) and rolling plus twisting (3D) resistance torques that mimic nonspherical shape and asymmetric contact pressure: the Constant torque model applies a torque proportional to the normal force, the Varying torque model (default) depends on the relative angular velocity and is capped at the constant torque value, or resistance can be switched off.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Rotational Resistance > Rotational resistance model; friction coefficients in Contact nodes (mur, mutw)

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Constant torque model, Varying torque model (default), None.

tools.example: // GUI: Granular Flow > Rotational Resistance = Constant torque model; Contact Between Grains > rolling friction 0.1
tools.notes: Rolling resistance strongly affects the angle of repose of spherical-grain models.

tools.name: Release (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Domain feature that inserts grains at specified release times (list, uniform, normal or lognormal distribution) at random positions or with a given density, with initial velocity, angular velocity and temperature. Overlap with existing grains and walls is checked, with retry attempts; released grain properties can be split by number, mass or volume fraction among species.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Release; Java: physics("gran").create("rel1", "Release", 3)

parameters.name: TimeDistributionFunction / rt
parameters.description: ListOfValues (rt), Uniform, Normal or Lognormal release times.

parameters.name: v0 / Tg0 / NAttempts
parameters.description: Initial velocity, temperature and release attempts.

tools.notes: Property keys verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Inlet (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Boundary release feature inserting grains with centers on selected boundaries (random, density-based, uniform distribution in 2D or projected plane grid in 3D), used for continuous feeding of hoppers, conveyors and mixers. The inlet boundaries are excluded from grain–wall interaction.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Inlet; Java: physics("gran").create("inl1", "GrainInlet", 2)

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: Random (default), Density, Uniform distribution (2D) or Projected plane grid (3D).

tools.notes: Java type id GrainInlet (verified).

tools.name: Release from Grid and Release from Data File (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Global release features placing grains at user-defined coordinates: Release from Grid uses lists or ranges of x, y, z coordinates (all combinations or specified combinations), and Release from Data File reads initial positions, velocities and auxiliary variables from a text file (one grain per row), e.g., from a previous packing simulation or CT data.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Release from Grid / Release from Data File; Java: physics("gran").create("relg1", "ReleaseGrid", -1); create("reldf1", "ReleaseFromDataFile", -1)

parameters.name: Initial coordinates
parameters.description: q_x,0, q_y,0, q_z,0 lists or range().

parameters.name: Data file
parameters.description: Text file with columns qx0 qy0 qz0 (and more); % starts comments.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("relg1", "ReleaseGrid", -1);
// GUI: Initial coordinates x: range(0,0.004,0.1), y: range(0,0.004,0.1), z: 0.2
tools.notes: Type ids verified as global features (dimension -1) in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Outlet (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Boundary condition deciding what happens to grains crossing selected boundaries: Disappear removes them (e.g., hopper outlets, sieve openings) and Pass through (default) lets them cross interior boundaries between domains, which are rigid walls otherwise. An Accumulator subnode can count grains leaving.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Outlet; Java: physics("gran").create("out1", "Outlet", 2)
tools.notes: For removing grains far from the region of interest the Bounding Box is faster than Disappear.

tools.name: Force and Torque (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Domain features applying user-defined external forces and torques to grains, for example fluid drag from a precomputed flow field, electrostatic or magnetic forces, vibration excitation or random forces using the grain index pidx. All forces and torques are summed with contact and gravity forces.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Force / Torque; Java: physics("gran").create("f1", "Force", 3); create("trq1", "Torque", 3)

parameters.name: Force F
parameters.description: Vector in N (can depend on grain variables and fields).

tools.notes: Grain variable names (velocity, diameter) are listed in the Grain statistics section of Insert Expression.

tools.name: Auxiliary Dependent Variable (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Global feature adding an extra ODE per grain integrated in time or along the grain trajectory, e.g., residence time (source 1, with respect to time), path length (source 1, along trajectory), number of wall collisions or accumulated energy. Initial values are set in release features.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Auxiliary Dependent Variable; Java: physics("gran").create("aux1", "AuxiliaryField", -1)

parameters.name: Integrate
parameters.description: With respect to time or Along grain trajectory.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("aux1", "AuxiliaryField", -1);
// GUI: Field variable name = tres, Source = 1, Integrate = With respect to time -> grain residence time in a mixer
tools.notes: Java type id AuxiliaryField verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Periodic boundaries along the x, y or z direction on planar source and destination boundaries: grains leaving one side re-enter on the other and interact with periodic images, allowing small representative sections of long chutes, shear cells or conveyors.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Periodic Condition; Java: physics("gran").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Source/destination boundaries
parameters.description: Planar, normals aligned with a coordinate axis.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: All boundaries normal to that axis must be selected.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2);
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").feature("pc1").selection().set(new int[]{1, 6});
tools.notes: Curved periodic boundaries are not supported.

tools.name: Grain Counter (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Domain feature collecting statistics about grains inside selected domains, filtered by release feature or grain species: number of grains transmitted, number at the final time, transmission probability and a logical expression for filtering plots. It measures discharge rates, separation efficiency and mixing indices.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Grain Counter; Java: physics("gran").create("gcnt1", "GrainCounter", 3)

parameters.name: Grain selection
parameters.description: Release feature (default All) or Grain properties.

parameters.name: Variables
parameters.description: Transmitted count, final count, transmission probability, filter expression.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("gcnt1", "GrainCounter", 3);
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").feature("gcnt1").selection().set(new int[]{4});
tools.notes: Type id verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Bounding Box (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Global feature defining a virtual rectangular box (from the geometry bounding box extended by 5 percent, or user-defined limits) outside which grains are removed, preventing escaped grains from slowing down the simulation. Only one Bounding Box per model.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Bounding Box; Java: physics("gran").create("bb1", "BoundingBox", -1)
tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("gran").create("bb1", "BoundingBox", -1);
// Application Library: Granular_Flow_Module/Flow_and_Material_Characterization/hopper_flow, Transport/screw_conveyor
tools.notes: Recommended over Outlet with Disappear for performance.

tools.name: Heat Source and Convective Heat Transfer (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Thermal features available when Compute grain temperature is on: Heat Source applies a user-defined source (W) per grain, and Convective Heat Transfer exchanges heat with a surrounding fluid using a heat transfer coefficient or a Nusselt-number correlation (lumped grain temperature, small Biot number). Together with conduction through contacts they model drying, heating in rotary kilns and cooling of hot powders.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Heat Source / Convective Heat Transfer; Java: physics("gran").create("hs1", "HeatSource", 3); create("cht1", "ConvectiveHeatTransfer", 3)

parameters.name: Heat source definition
parameters.description: Specify heat transfer coefficient or Specify Nusselt number (default).

tools.notes: The fluid is assumed not to affect grain motion in Convective Heat Transfer.

tools.name: Accumulators and Force Accumulator (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Features that transfer grain information to the mesh: Accumulator (Boundary), a subnode of Wall or Outlet, accumulates a user source per wall element whenever grains hit it (density or count); Force Accumulator accumulates the normal contact force on wall elements (wall loads, wear); Accumulator (Domain) accumulates grain properties per domain element (over elements or elements and time), e.g., local solid fraction.
tools.usage: Granular Flow > Wall > Accumulator / Force Accumulator; Domains > Accumulator; Java: physics("gran").feature("wp1").create("facc1", "BoundaryForceAccumulator", 2); create("dacc1", "DomainAccumulator", 3)

parameters.name: Source R
parameters.description: Quantity added per grain hit or per grain in element.

tools.notes: Type ids BoundaryAccumulator, BoundaryForceAccumulator (Wall subnodes) and DomainAccumulator verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Grain Dataset and Grain Trajectories Plot (Granular Flow)
tools.description: Results tools for DEM: the Grain dataset (created automatically) holds grain positions for plotting and for evaluating counts or fractions in selections; Grain Trajectories plots show grains colored by velocity, species or release feature (with a filter subnode), and grain data can also be shown as Poincaré maps or phase portraits.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > More Datasets > Grain; Plot group > Grain Trajectories; Java: model.result().dataset().create("grn1", "Grain"); plot group feature "GrainTrajectories"

parameters.name: Grain dataset selections
parameters.description: Restrict to domains/boundaries to count grains.

parameters.name: Grain Trajectories
parameters.description: Point or line rendering, coloring and filter (GrainTrajectoriesFilter).

tools.notes: Type names (Grain, GrainTrajectories, GrainTrajectoriesFilter) taken from the index of the COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Time Step and Explicit Solver for DEM (gran.ts)
tools.description: Granular Flow uses only explicit time integration (default classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta). A suggested stable time step is stored in the global variable gran.ts, based on the spring-mass period for the linear elastic model or the Rayleigh time step (smallest grain radius, lowest density, highest shear modulus) for Hertz models, with a 0.2 safety factor; the solver uses it automatically but users should verify it.
tools.usage: Study > Time Dependent (explicit Runge–Kutta); time step = gran.ts

parameters.name: Values of dependent variables
parameters.description: Chain studies (fill, settle, then flow) using a previous solution.

tools.notes: Soft grains (lower E) allow larger time steps; reducing E is a common DEM speed-up if bulk behavior is preserved.

tools.name: Grain Statistics Variables (Granular Flow: pidx, grf, rti)
tools.description: Special per-grain variables of the Granular Flow interface used in expressions and results: grain index gran.pidx (unique per grain, useful for random forces rn(pidx,t)), grain release feature gran.grf (numbered per release node, for mixing visualization), release time gran.rti, plus grain position, velocity, diameter, mass and optional coordination numbers gran.Ng and gran.Nw.
tools.usage: Results > Insert Expression > Grain statistics; prefix gran.
tools.example:
// color grains by release feature in a mixer: Grain Trajectories > Color expression = gran.grf
// Application Library: Granular_Flow_Module/Mixing_and_Separation/ribbon_mixer
tools.notes: Variables are prefixed by the interface name (gran, gran2, ...).
